grade.basis: Blind assessment before opening either existing review. Inspected all 28 PDF pages (three introductory pages and all 25 score pages), treating all three movements as one approximately ten-minute work. Viola 4 is the principal technical bottleneck rather than the highest line: Loekie Blues printed pp.5-6, bars 61-89 has the mobile chromatic counterline and accented rising figures; Slow blues song pp.12-14, bars 29-46 has sustained chromatic sixteenth-note runs, mixed slur/staccato, leaps, and displaced accents, shared closely with Viola 3; De Stille pp.18 and 24 adds chromatic four-note tuplets against compound pulse. All eight staves are printed in treble clef, including low ledger-line C-string material; this is a reading burden, not evidence of high-position playing. Overall register runs approximately C3 to F5; Viola 4 stays roughly C4-Eb5. The upper lines and Viola 5 reach higher but chiefly use simpler melody. Compound 6/8, offbeat entries, ties over beats, alternating pizzicato/arco, mute changes, chromatic blues intonation and precise dynamic/articulation coordination support upper-intermediate level 3. Dotted-quarter 116/66/124 gives brisk outer-movement eighth notes but the densest sustained sixteenths occur in the slow movement. No pervasive double stops, harmonics, advanced bowing or extreme register; eight players alone does not lift the grade. Teaching estimate anchored to supplied level 3 ABRSM6/RCM7 band, not an official syllabus placement.

findings.finding: IMSLP score index 559349, Version A for eight violas, complete local 28-page score. Contents gives Loekie Blues dotted-quarter 116, Slow Blues Song 66, De Stille 124, total about ten minutes. Composer preface emphasizes careful articulation and timing in each part and ensemble; notation confirms Viola 4/3 carry harder inner contrapuntal figuration than the higher Viola 1 melody.
